caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.
raw_response:
This line plot illustrates Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for four model variants: Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. The x-axis is labeled "Number of completions (k)" and employs a base-2 logarithmic scale ranging from 2^0 to 2^8, with tick marks at every consecutive power of 2. The y-axis is labeled "Coverage" and uses a linear scale with tick marks at 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8. The "Llama-3B" data series is represented by a solid dark blue line with circular markers, starting at approximately 0.43 at 2^0 and increasing monotonically to reach about 0.92 at 2^8. The "Llama-3B + FT" series is shown as a dotted dark green line with triangular markers, which closely overlaps the Llama-3B line throughout the plot, also starting near 0.43 and ending near 0.92. The "Llama-1B" series is depicted by a solid light blue line with circular markers, beginning at roughly 0.25 at 2^0 and rising steadily to approximately 0.86 at 2^8. Finally, the "Llama-1B + FT" series is a dotted light green line with triangular markers that closely tracks and overlaps the Llama-1B line, starting at about 0.25 and ending at roughly 0.86.
